messages.author: e7a71d967e60bb41
messages.subject: Problem with Fill Color
parts:
Dear All,
I must be misunderstanding something basic.
Please consider the snippet at the end of the email. The idea is to
generate a simple histogram, where in each bin I see the contribution of
two kinds of data parametrized by the value of the 'is_facebook' parameter.
However, this is not what I get, so I am puzzled. Another thing I am
after is to overlay the two histograms (generated by classifying the
$weight data according to their is_facebook parameter (0 or 1)).
Any help is appreciated.
Cheers

Lorenzo


#############################################
#############################################

library(ggplot2)
library(Cairo)

threshold <- 15 #i.e. 5 min

eswc <-
read.table("http://dl.dropbox.com/u/5685598/eswc2009_f2f_edges.dat",
header=FALSE)
names(eswc) <- c("ID1","unknown", "ON/OFF", "ID2",
"intermittency","is_face-2_face", "is_facebook","type", "weight" )


eswc_sel <- eswc[which(eswc$weight>=threshold), ]

gpl <- ggplot(eswc_sel,aes(x=weight, y=..count.., fill=is_facebook))+
geom_histogram(binwidth=0.15,origin=log10(15))+
# geom_histogram(data=mw_fb, aes(x=mw_fb,
y=..count../sum(..count..)),binwidth=0.15, colour="red",
fill="white",origin=log10(15))+
## scale_x_log10() +
scale_x_log10()+
#scale_y_continuous(limits=c(0,.3))+
## scale_y_continuous(trans = "log10")+

xlab(expression(paste("weight")))+
ylab(expression(paste("P(weight)")))+
opts(title = expression(paste("ESWC, All links")))+
opts(plot.title = theme_text(size = 20))+
opts(axis.title.x = theme_text(size = 20))+
opts(axis.title.y = theme_text(size = 20, angle=90))+
opts(axis.text.x = theme_text(size=15, colour="black",vjust=1))+
opts(axis.text.y = theme_text(size=15, colour="black", hjust=1))

fn <- paste("test-facebook-vs-no-facebook.pdf")

CairoPDF(fn)
print(gpl)
dev.off()

messages.author: b756a7daa2c2aa6d
messages.subject: Re: Problem with Fill Color
parts:
Hi Lorenzo,

The problem is that is_facebook is continuous, so get a histogram for
each value, you need to either convert it to a factor, or use group =
is_facebook to explicitly define the grouping.

Hadley
